attack_mechanism: A fault on `cv32e40p_top.core_i.boot_addr_i` can substitute or replay a CSR instruction so that the combinational CSR block observes a non-READ operation. Exception, debug, and branch redirection select the instruction presented to the decoder and therefore the CSR operation entering the pipeline. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.boot_addr_i` changes that fetch/decode control route before it reaches `csr_op_i`; the active mux/state branches are selected by `cv32e40p_top.core_i.if_stage_i.aligner_i.branch_i`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.if_stage_i.aligner_i.rst_n`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.if_stage_i.rst_n`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.controller_i.branch_taken_ex_i`, and the remaining path guards. Signal propagation follows `cv32e40p_top.core_i.boot_addr_i -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.if_stage_i.branch_addr_n -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.trigger_match_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. `csr_we_int` asserts for an instruction that was not the intended control-flow successor, corrupting protected CSR state.

A fault on `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op` during CSR decode can exchange READ with WRITE/SET/CLEAR, or convert a legitimate write into READ. In the CSR combinational block, `csr_we_int` defaults to one and is cleared only when `csr_op_i == CSR_OP_READ`; WRITE, SET, and CLEAR therefore retain the write enable. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op` generates, transports, or selects `csr_op_i` on this decode path; the active mux/state branches are selected by `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.deassert_we_i`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. Signal propagation follows `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. The primary write-enable is spuriously asserted or suppressed, corrupting CSR state or dropping an intended security-state update.

Forcing `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op` toward the READ encoding for that cycle clears `csr_we_int` even though the instruction was authorized to modify the CSR. A legitimate WRITE, SET, or CLEAR depends on `csr_op_i` remaining different from `CSR_OP_READ` throughout combinational evaluation. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op` lies on the operation-code path that keeps `csr_we_int` at its default value of one. Signal propagation follows `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. The required privilege, interrupt, or debug-state update is silently lost, leaving security state stale.
